I am a postdoctoral fellow in the laboratory of Eric Olson at UT Southwestern
Medical Center, where I study how the immune system shapes the regenerating
heart. Newborn mammalian hearts can rebuild themselves after injury; adult
hearts cannot. I work on the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway and the immunosuppressive
environment that this regenerative window depends on — research supported
since 2025 by an American Heart Association Career Development Award.

I completed my PhD with Michael Sieweke at the Centre d'Immunologie de
Marseille-Luminy and the Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine in Berlin,
on the molecular mechanisms that allow tissue-resident macrophages to renew
themselves, and a Diploma in Molecular Medicine at the University of Freiburg.

Alongside research I chair the webinar committee of the International Society
for Regenerative Biology for the Americas, and I speak about the path of a
Latin American scientist in STEM.
